tasks.title: Retell the Seedling Experiment
tasks.scenario: Your lab partner was absent for the bean seedling experiment. Retell what the class did and found so your partner can start the lab report.
tasks.prompt: Listen to the class recording. Then retell the experiment in order: what the class tested, what they did, what they found, and what they concluded.

turns.speaker: Ms. Okafor
turns.text: Yesterday we tested whether light changes how bean seedlings grow. First, we planted four bean seeds in four identical cups of soil. Next, we put two cups on the sunny windowsill and two cups inside a dark cabinet. Every morning each cup got 50 milliliters of water.

turns.speaker: Dani
turns.text: On day seven we measured the stems with a ruler. The windowsill seedlings were about eight centimeters tall and dark green. The cabinet seedlings were taller, about thirteen centimeters, but they were thin and pale yellow.

turns.speaker: Ms. Okafor
turns.text: Right. In the dark, seedlings stretch quickly to search for light. But without light they cannot make chlorophyll, so they turn pale. Finally, we concluded that plants need light to grow healthy, not just tall.

planner.label: What they tested
planner.hint: Say what the class wanted to find out.

planner.label: What they did
planner.hint: Use first, next, and every morning.

planner.label: What they found
planner.hint: Compare the windowsill and cabinet seedlings with numbers.

planner.label: What they concluded
planner.hint: Finish with the big idea about light.

vocab.def: a very young plant that has just sprouted from a seed
vocab.es: plántula: planta muy joven que acaba de brotar de la semilla

vocab.def: the green material in plants that uses light to make food

successCriteria: I tell the events in the same order the recording did.
I use sequence words such as first, next, and finally.
I use at least two numbers or measurements from the recording.
I end with what the class concluded.

listenFor: Sequence words (first, next, on day seven, finally)
Past-tense verbs for completed steps (planted, measured, turned)
Contrast of the two groups with measurements
A conclusion that says why, not only what
teacher.followUp: Why were the cabinet seedlings taller if they were less healthy?

frames: First, the class planted ___ and put them ___.
On day seven, the seedlings on the ___ were ___, but the seedlings in the ___ were ___.
This happened because ___.
In conclusion, the class learned that ___.
guided.model: The class tested whether light changes how bean seedlings grow. First, they planted four seeds in identical cups. Next, they put two cups on the sunny windowsill and two in a dark cabinet, and they gave each cup fifty milliliters of water every morning. On day seven, they measured the stems. The windowsill seedlings were about eight centimeters tall and dark green. The cabinet seedlings were taller, about thirteen centimeters, but they were thin and pale yellow. That happened because plants in the dark stretch to find light and cannot make chlorophyll. In conclusion, the class learned that plants need light to grow healthy, not only tall.

tasks.title: Compare Two River Civilizations
tasks.scenario: You are recording a class podcast about early civilizations. Compare how rivers shaped life in ancient Egypt and ancient Mesopotamia.
tasks.prompt: Read the two paragraphs. Then compare the two civilizations: say how they were alike, and how their rivers led to differences in farming and government.

text: Ancient Egypt grew along the Nile River. Each summer the Nile flooded at a regular time and left rich, dark silt on the fields. Because farmers could predict the flood, they could plan when to plant and when to harvest. Egypt was united under one ruler, the pharaoh, and people recorded events in hieroglyphs.

Ancient Mesopotamia grew between the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers. These rivers flooded at unpredictable times, and sometimes the floods destroyed crops and homes. Farmers dug irrigation canals to control the water. Mesopotamia was organized into separate city-states, such as Ur, each with its own ruler, and scribes pressed cuneiform into clay tablets.

guided.model: Both ancient Egypt and ancient Mesopotamia developed near rivers, and both had farming and writing. However, the Nile flooded at a regular time, but the Tigris and Euphrates flooded unpredictably. As a result, Egyptian farmers could plan their planting, while farmers in Mesopotamia had to dig irrigation canals to control the water. Another difference is government. Egypt was united under one ruler, the pharaoh, whereas Mesopotamia was divided into separate city-states, each with its own ruler. These differences show that a river can shape both how people farm and how they organize their society.

guided.model: Cup 2, the open cup in the sunny window, lost the most water. It started with 100 milliliters and ended with only 62. This happened because of evaporation, which is when liquid water changes into water vapor and goes into the air. The cup in the sun lost more than the cup on the shady shelf because the sun gave the water more heat energy, so more water molecules escaped as vapor. The covered cup stayed almost full, with 99 milliliters, because the plastic wrap trapped the water vapor, so it could not leave the cup. This shows that heat and open air both increase evaporation.

vocab.def: the movement of many people from one place to live in another
vocab.es: migración: movimiento de muchas personas de un lugar a otro para vivir

vocab.def: a hard condition that makes people want to leave a place
vocab.es: factor de expulsión: condición difícil que hace que la gente quiera irse de un lugar

vocab.def: something attractive that makes people want to move to a place
vocab.es: factor de atracción: algo atractivo que hace que la gente quiera mudarse a un lugar

successCriteria: I describe the change in the graph with two numbers.
I name at least one push factor and one pull factor.
I use because of or as a result to link causes to growth.
I use history words correctly.

listenFor: Causal chains (because of..., which led to...)
Distinction between push and pull categories
Accurate use of graph evidence
Academic vocabulary (migration, segregation, wages)
teacher.followUp: How might the move have changed the neighborhoods people left behind?

frames: The graph shows that between ___ and ___, the population grew from ___ to ___.
One push factor was ___, which made people want to ___.
One pull factor was ___, so ___.
Because of both push and pull factors, ___.
guided.model: The graph shows that between 1910 and 1940, the Black population of Chicago grew from about 44,000 to about 278,000. One push factor was segregation and violence in the South, together with crop damage that made farming hard, which made many families want to leave. One pull factor was the demand for workers in Chicago's factories and meatpacking plants, especially when World War One slowed immigration from Europe. People also heard from relatives and in newspapers that wages were higher and schools were open to their children. Because of both push and pull factors, hundreds of thousands of people made the journey north.

tasks.title: Speak at the School Board Meeting
tasks.scenario: The school board is voting on whether your middle school should start at 8:30 a.m. instead of 7:30 a.m. You have two minutes to speak at the meeting.
tasks.prompt: Take a position for or against the later start time. Use at least two pieces of evidence from the table, and respond to one concern someone might have.

table.caption: Survey of students at two middle schools
rows: Average hours of sleep on school nights
Students who say they feel awake in first class

planner.label: My position
planner.hint: Say clearly: I support or I oppose.

planner.label: First piece of evidence
planner.hint: Use a number from the table.

planner.label: Second piece of evidence
planner.hint: Use a different row.

planner.label: A concern and my answer
planner.hint: Some people say ... However ...

planner.label: My closing request
planner.hint: Tell the board what to do.

vocab.def: facts or numbers that show a claim is true
vocab.es: evidencia: datos o números que muestran que una afirmación es verdadera

vocab.def: to disagree with a plan or idea
vocab.es: oponerse: estar en desacuerdo con un plan o una idea

vocab.def: to say that something is a good choice
vocab.es: recomendar: decir que algo es una buena opción

successCriteria: I state my position in the first sentence.
I support it with at least two numbers from the table.
I respond to a different point of view with however or although.
I end with a clear request.

listenFor: Clear claim stated up front
Evidence introduced with attribution (according to the survey)
Counterargument and rebuttal language (some people say..., however)
Persuasive register appropriate for a formal meeting
teacher.followUp: What other data would make your argument stronger?

frames: I support / oppose the later start time because ___.
According to the survey, students at ___ get ___ hours of sleep, compared with ___ at ___.
In addition, ___ percent of students at ___ feel awake, but only ___ percent at ___.
For these reasons, I ask the board to ___.
guided.model: I support the later start time because students learn better when they are rested. According to the survey, students at Hillcrest Middle, which starts at 8:30, get 7.6 hours of sleep, compared with only 6.8 hours at Lakeside Middle. In addition, 64 percent of Hillcrest students feel awake in first class, but only 38 percent at Lakeside. They also have fewer late arrivals, 27 per week instead of 42. Some people worry that a later start will make after-school activities end later. However, the schedule can be adjusted, and good sleep matters more. For these reasons, I ask the board to vote yes.

tasks.title: Argue for a Class Fundraiser
tasks.scenario: Your class needs money for a trip, and your teacher asks groups to recommend one fundraiser. You will present your recommendation to the class before the vote.
tasks.prompt: Choose one plan and argue that it is the best. Compute the profit (money earned minus cost to start) for your plan, compare it with at least one other plan, and mention one other factor.

table.caption: Three fundraiser plans for the class trip

planner.label: My choice
planner.hint: Name the plan you recommend.

planner.label: Profit for my plan
planner.hint: Subtract the cost from the money earned.

planner.label: Comparison
planner.hint: Compare your profit to another plan.

planner.label: Another factor
planner.hint: Think about time, people, or risk.

planner.label: Closing
planner.hint: Restate your recommendation.

vocab.def: money left after you subtract the cost from the money earned
vocab.es: ganancia: dinero que queda después de restar el costo del dinero recibido

vocab.def: a person who helps without being paid
vocab.es: voluntario: persona que ayuda sin recibir pago

vocab.def: looking at how two things are alike or different
vocab.es: en comparación con: observar en qué se parecen o se diferencian dos cosas

successCriteria: I name one plan and give a reason in my first sentence.
I compute the profit correctly and say the numbers aloud.
I compare my plan with another plan.
I include a factor that is not only about money.

listenFor: Correct arithmetic stated aloud (320 minus 65 equals 255)
Comparatives with quantities (85 dollars more)
Reasoned weighing of trade-offs (although, but)
Concluding sentence with therefore or so
teacher.followUp: What would make you change your recommendation?

frames: I recommend the ___ because ___.
Its profit is ___ minus ___, which equals ___.
Compared with the ___, which has a profit of ___, it earns ___ more / less.
Therefore, our class should choose ___.
guided.model: I recommend the bake sale because it earns the most money. Its profit is 320 dollars minus 65 dollars, which equals 255 dollars. Compared with the car wash, which has a profit of 170 dollars, the bake sale earns 85 dollars more. Another important factor is the work. The bake sale takes ten hours, but only eight volunteers are needed, so we can take turns and no one has to work too long. Candy sales are the cheapest to start, but they take three weeks and earn only 150 dollars in profit. Therefore, our class should choose the bake sale.

tasks.title: Argue for a Reading Format
tasks.scenario: Your ELA teacher is planning next semester's required reading and asks students what formats to include. You will share your opinion with the class.
tasks.prompt: Argue which formats the teacher should include. Use the graph as evidence, and also respond to a concern that some formats may be easier but less challenging.

chart.title: Students who finished the last assigned book, by format

planner.label: My position
planner.hint: Which format or mix of formats do you recommend?

planner.label: Evidence from the graph
planner.hint: Use two percents.

planner.label: My reasoning
planner.hint: Explain why finishing the book matters.

planner.label: A concern and my answer
planner.hint: Some people think ... but ...

vocab.def: the form in which a story or text is presented
vocab.es: formato: la forma en que se presenta un cuento o un texto

vocab.def: given by a teacher as required work
vocab.es: asignado: dado por un maestro como tarea obligatoria

vocab.def: having many parts or ideas; not simple
vocab.es: complejo: con muchas partes o ideas; no simple

successCriteria: I state which formats I recommend in the first sentence.
I use at least two percents from the graph.
I explain why the evidence matters.
I answer a different opinion with however or although.

listenFor: A clear stance with a reason
Evidence language (the graph shows, according to)
Counterclaim with a concessive structure (although, some people think)
Academic vocabulary (format, analyze, complex)
teacher.followUp: Finishing a book is one measure. What other evidence would show that students learned from it?

frames: I believe the teacher should include ___ because ___.
The graph shows that ___ percent of students finished the ___, but only ___ percent finished the ___.
Some people think ___; however, ___.
That is why I recommend ___.
guided.model: I believe the teacher should include a mix of formats, especially graphic novels and audiobooks, because more students finish them. The graph shows that 81 percent of students finished the graphic novel and 73 percent finished the audiobook, but only 54 percent finished the regular novel. This matters because students who finish a book can discuss it and write about it, but students who stop reading cannot. Some people think graphic novels are too easy. However, they include complex characters and themes, and students still have to analyze the pictures and the words. That is why I recommend using different formats, along with one traditional novel.

tasks.title: Discuss Why the Ice Melted Faster
tasks.scenario: In science class, your group's ice cubes melted at different speeds. Your partner Camila has a different idea about why. Discuss it so your group can write one explanation.
tasks.prompt: Listen to the lab recording. Then explain your idea about why the ice melted faster on the metal tray. Respond to your partner's questions with evidence.

turns.speaker: Mr. Chen
turns.text: Here are your group's results. The ice cube on the metal tray melted in four minutes. The ice cube on the plastic tray took nine minutes. The room was 21 degrees Celsius, and both trays sat on the same desk for an hour before the test.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Both ice cubes started at the same size. The metal tray feels colder than the plastic tray when I touch it, but the ice still melted faster on the metal tray.

planner.label: My explanation
planner.hint: Say your idea in one sentence.

planner.label: Evidence from the results
planner.hint: Use the times and the room temperature.

planner.label: The science idea
planner.hint: Use conductor or insulator.

planner.label: Answer my partner
planner.hint: Use I see your point, but ... or I agree because ...

vocab.def: a material that lets heat move through it easily
vocab.es: conductor: material por el que el calor se mueve fácilmente

vocab.def: a material that does not let heat move through it easily
vocab.es: aislante: material por el que el calor no se mueve fácilmente

vocab.def: to move from one place or object to another
vocab.es: transferir: pasar de un lugar u objeto a otro

successCriteria: I give an explanation and use evidence from the results.
I use science words correctly.
I respond to my partner's question instead of repeating my idea.
I use polite language to disagree or to agree.

turns.say: I think the metal tray was just warmer than the plastic tray. Do you agree?
But metal feels cold when I touch it. Doesn't that mean the metal is colder, so it should melt the ice slower?
Okay, that makes sense. How could we test your idea in another experiment?

listenFor: Claim with evidence and scientific vocabulary
Polite disagreement phrases (I see your point, but...)
Responding directly to the partner's challenge
Proposing a testable change (a third material, a thermometer)
teacher.followUp: Why does a metal spoon in hot soup get hot, but a wooden spoon does not?

frames: I think the ice melted faster on the metal tray because ___.
The results show that ___ melted in ___ minutes, while ___ took ___.
Metal is a ___, which means ___.
I see your point about ___, but ___.
guided.model: I think the ice melted faster on the metal tray because metal is a conductor, so it moves heat from the room into the ice quickly. The results show that the ice on the metal tray melted in four minutes, while the ice on the plastic tray took nine. Both trays were the same temperature as the room, 21 degrees Celsius, so one tray was not warmer. Plastic is an insulator, which means it slows down the transfer of heat. I see your point that metal feels colder, but that is because it pulls heat away from my hand quickly, not because it is actually colder.

tasks.title: Discuss the Empty Lot
tasks.scenario: Your civics class is role-playing a town meeting. Your partner Rosa will question your position on how the town should use an empty lot.
tasks.prompt: Listen to the town meeting. Then decide whether the lot should become a park or a branch library, and defend your choice in a discussion with Rosa.

turns.speaker: Ms. Alvarez
turns.text: The empty lot on Maple Street has been unused for six years. The town has enough money for one project: a park with a playground, or a branch library.

turns.speaker: Mr. Brooks
turns.text: I live next to the lot. A library would help students with homework, but it would bring more traffic. A park would be quieter, though it can be noisy in the afternoon.

turns.speaker: Ms. Alvarez
turns.text: A survey of 400 residents found that 58 percent want the park and 42 percent want the library.

planner.label: My position
planner.hint: Park or branch library?

planner.label: My strongest reason
planner.hint: Use information from the meeting.

planner.label: A second reason
planner.hint: Think about who benefits.

planner.label: Answer my partner
planner.hint: Respond to her question with evidence.

vocab.def: a person who lives in a place
vocab.es: residente: persona que vive en un lugar

vocab.def: to help or be good for someone
vocab.es: beneficiar: ayudar o ser bueno para alguien

vocab.def: cars and other vehicles moving on roads
vocab.es: tráfico: vehículos que circulan por las calles

successCriteria: I state my choice and give reasons from the meeting.
I use the survey numbers accurately.
I respond to Rosa's questions, not only repeat my first point.
I use a concession such as I understand ... but.

turns.say: I think the park is best because most people voted for it. Do you agree?
But a park is free for everyone, and a library needs workers and books. Isn't that a lot more expensive?
Okay. If the town could only choose one, what would be the fairest way to decide?

listenFor: Position with reasons tied to the meeting
Concession language (I understand..., but...)
Accurate use of percents and totals
Fairness and community vocabulary
teacher.followUp: Is the majority always right when a town makes a decision?

frames: I think the town should build ___ because ___.
According to the survey, ___ percent of the ___ residents want ___.
I understand your concern about ___, but ___.
To sum up, ___.
guided.model: I think the town should build the branch library because it would help more people for a longer time. According to the survey, 58 percent of the 400 residents want the park, so the park is a little more popular, but 42 percent want the library, which is still 168 people. Another reason is that a library would benefit students who need a quiet place and computers for homework. I understand your concern about traffic, but we can build parking and a bus stop to reduce the problem. To sum up, a library gives many people a place to learn, and a park can be added in another place later.

tasks.title: Discuss Two Discounts
tasks.scenario: Two students disagree about the price of a jacket after two discounts. Your partner Andre is not sure who is right, and you will explain the math to him.
tasks.prompt: Listen to Marcus and Lena. Decide who is correct, explain how you know, and answer Andre's questions.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: The jacket costs forty dollars. It is twenty-five percent off, and then there is another ten percent off at the register. Twenty-five plus ten is thirty-five, so it is thirty-five percent off, and I pay twenty-six dollars.

turns.speaker: Lena
turns.text: I do not think the discounts add together. Twenty-five percent off forty dollars is thirty dollars. Then ten percent off thirty dollars is three dollars, so I pay twenty-seven dollars.

planner.label: Who is correct
planner.hint: Say who is right and the final price.

planner.label: Why the percents do not add
planner.hint: Say what each percent is taken from.

planner.label: Show it with numbers
planner.hint: Walk through the dollar amounts.

planner.label: Answer my partner
planner.hint: Respond to Andre's questions.

vocab.def: an amount taken off the regular price
vocab.es: descuento: cantidad que se resta del precio normal

vocab.def: a part out of 100 of a certain amount
vocab.es: porcentaje de: una parte de cada 100 de una cantidad determinada

vocab.def: the price before any discount
vocab.es: precio original: el precio antes de cualquier descuento

successCriteria: I decide who is correct and say the final price.
I explain what each percent is taken from.
I say the dollar amounts aloud as evidence.
I answer my partner's question directly.

turns.say: Marcus has a point, though. Twenty-five and ten make thirty-five. Why wouldn't that work?
So is ten percent of thirty the same as ten percent of forty?
Can you think of another example where adding the percents gives the wrong answer?

listenFor: Mathematical reasoning expressed in complete sentences
Precise referents (of the new price, of the original price)
Numbers said aloud correctly
Responding to the partner's challenge with a new example
teacher.followUp: Would the final price change if the 10 percent discount came first?

frames: I think ___ is correct because ___.
The second discount is taken from ___, not from ___.
For example, ___ percent of ___ is ___, but ___ percent of ___ is ___.
So the final price is ___.
guided.model: I think Lena is correct because the second discount is taken from the new price, not from the original price. After the first discount, the jacket costs thirty dollars. Ten percent of thirty is three dollars, but ten percent of forty is four dollars, so the second discount is smaller than Marcus thought. If we add the percents, Marcus takes off fourteen dollars, but Lena only takes off thirteen dollars in total. So the final price is twenty-seven dollars, not twenty-six. In general, two percent discounts in a row are not the same as one discount that adds the two percents.
